nodes.name: One Suitcase
nodes.journal_entry: I arrived at the Harmon property with one suitcase and fifty-six days ahead of me. Frank shook my hand. Ryan grinned like I was a dare. Jake smiled at his shoes.

nodes.name: Unpacking
nodes.journal_entry: Small room. Thin walls. Through one wall — Jake's pencil. Through the floor — Frank's dishes. The mattress smells like someone else's laundry detergent. Home for fifty-six days.

nodes.name: The Bathroom Door
nodes.journal_entry: The bathroom lock doesn't work. Jake was inside. He didn't stammer or blush. 'Knock.' One word. Like I'm furniture. Like I don't exist.

nodes.name: The Bus or the Truck
nodes.journal_entry: Getting to town: $2 bus ride, forty minutes. Or Ryan's truck, fifteen minutes, free. Nothing is free.

nodes.name: The Transfer's Delayed
nodes.journal_entry: Mom called. Transfer delayed. She sounded tired. I told her I was fine. I'm not fine.

nodes.name: Thirteen Dollars
nodes.journal_entry: $400. Monthly expenses: $385. Surplus: $13. For ten weeks. Frank offered cleaning work — $20 per session. It's not enough. But it's something.

nodes.name: Routines
nodes.journal_entry: One week. I know Frank's coffee schedule, Jake's humming, Ryan's unpredictability. I know which floorboards creak. The house is teaching me its language.

nodes.name: The Pencil Stops
nodes.journal_entry: Jake looked at me today. Actually looked. His pencil stopped mid-line and he tore the page out. Later, in the hallway: 'I could draw you. This afternoon. If you're not busy.' Three weeks of nothing. Then that.

nodes.name: Something Shifts
nodes.journal_entry: Something changed today. The way he looked at me — or the way I noticed him looking. I don't know which is worse. I don't know which I want.

nodes.name: The Creek
nodes.journal_entry: Ryan at the creek. Shirt off. I couldn't look away. He knew.

nodes.name: The Hallway at Midnight
nodes.journal_entry: 2 AM. Sleep shirt. He looked at the hem, then my face. Just for a second. I felt it.

nodes.name: The Reference Photo
nodes.journal_entry: He asked for a reference photo. For the drawing, he said. I sent it. The light on my collarbone, he said. He noticed the light.

nodes.name: Drawing Sessions
nodes.journal_entry: Jake drew my hands today. When he showed me, I saw things I didn't know he noticed — the chip in my thumbnail, the freckle below my ear. He sees things nobody else sees.

nodes.name: The Hand on the Knee
nodes.journal_entry: Ryan's hand on my knee in the truck. I had three seconds to decide. Whatever I chose — that's the direction now. No going back.

nodes.name: Wrong Turn
nodes.journal_entry: Ryan missed the turn today. Stopped at a site that isn't Frank's. Talked to someone I couldn't see. 'Wrong turn.' It wasn't.

nodes.name: Two Weeks
nodes.journal_entry: Phone call. He pulled over, stepped out. I heard fragments through the truck door. 'Two weeks.' 'Hold the spot.' He didn't explain.

nodes.name: Under the Seat
nodes.journal_entry: Map under the truck seat. A city circled in red. A job offer — his own crew, real money. He's leaving. Before Mom comes back.

nodes.name: Twenty-Three and Stuck
nodes.journal_entry: He's 23 and stuck. Dad's house, dad's jobs, dad's roads. The scar was the day he knew he'd be doing this forever. The offer is real. He leaves before Mom comes back.

nodes.name: Candlelight
nodes.journal_entry: Storm. Candlelight. Ryan told the real story of his scar — eighteen, scared, thought his arm was broken. Frank drove him to the ER without a word. 'You were fine.' 'I know. That's why you didn't talk.' For one evening, nobody was performing.

nodes.name: Come With Me
nodes.journal_entry: 'Come with me.' Not blackmail. Not leverage. A man in a truck asking someone to choose him. The only honest question anyone in this house has asked me.

nodes.name: Engine Running
nodes.journal_entry: Dawn. The truck was packed. The engine was running. What happened next changed everything.

nodes.name: The Office Door
nodes.journal_entry: $25 per session. Three times a week. Behind a door that locks. The money changes everything. The door changes something else.

nodes.name: The Swimming Hole
nodes.journal_entry: Found the creek. Fifteen minutes through the trees. Cold water, smooth rocks, nobody watching. The one place that's mine.

nodes.name: The Portfolio
nodes.journal_entry: Jake showed me his portfolio. Not the ones of me — the real work. The creek, the workshop, Frank's hands on a coffee mug. They're actually good. He looked at me like my opinion was the only one that mattered.

nodes.name: Crossing the Line
nodes.journal_entry: I flirted. Deliberately. Not accidental, not a misunderstanding. I chose to cross that line. And I liked what I saw on the other side.

nodes.name: The First Tease
nodes.journal_entry: I did it on purpose. Not accidental, not a misunderstanding. I dressed for it. I positioned for it. I watched the reaction. And I liked what I saw.

nodes.name: Matching Energy
nodes.journal_entry: I flirted with Ryan. Not his usual dares — I dared back. His grin froze. Then cracked wider.

nodes.name: The Spot
nodes.journal_entry: Gym. Spotting him. I leaned over the bench and let gravity do the work. His rep stuttered. I didn't step back.

nodes.name: Pulled Across
nodes.journal_entry: He pulled me across the bench seat. No preamble. No asking. Ryan kisses like he drives — fast, certain, no brakes.

nodes.name: The Silence
nodes.journal_entry: I stopped working and just looked at him. He felt it. His pen stopped. Neither of us said anything. We didn't need to.

nodes.name: The Floor
nodes.journal_entry: Short shorts. On my knees. I heard his boots stop behind me. Three seconds. Then faster. I smiled at the floor.

nodes.name: Whiskey and This Can't Happen
nodes.journal_entry: 2 AM. Kitchen. Whiskey. He kissed me like a man drowning. His hand gripped the chair, not me. Because if he held me he wouldn't stop.

nodes.name: You're Never Around
nodes.journal_entry: 'You're never around anymore.' He told me he's leaving and I haven't said a word about it since. He's right. I've been pretending it's not happening.

nodes.name: The First
nodes.journal_entry: The first kiss. I'll remember who, where, how it tasted, forever. The point of no return — I passed it and didn't even slow down.

nodes.name: Under the Mattress
nodes.journal_entry: Found Jake's hidden drawings. Me sleeping. Me in a towel. Poses I never held for him. The sweet one has been watching. What I said next changed everything.

nodes.name: The Poses Deepen
nodes.journal_entry: The poses have changed. He asks me to adjust — lower the strap, turn toward the light. Each session pulls us deeper. The drawings are becoming something we can't take back.

nodes.name: The Angle Photo
nodes.journal_entry: He needed another reference. My waist, he said. I sent the mirror pic. He looked at it for ten minutes. Then he drew all night.

nodes.name: The Strap
nodes.journal_entry: The strap. He asked about a shadow and I lowered it myself. His pencil slowed. We both pretended it was still about the drawing.

nodes.name: The Towel Photo
nodes.journal_entry: I sent it by accident. That's what I told him. He didn't delete it. I didn't ask him to. Not really.

nodes.name: Without Anything
nodes.journal_entry: I took off the shirt without being asked. He drew me like I was the most important thing. I was bare and I didn't feel naked. I felt seen.

nodes.name: The Underwear Photo
nodes.journal_entry: No accident this time. No excuse. I chose to send it. He asked me to come to his room. The drawings aren't art anymore.

nodes.name: The Pencil Drops
nodes.journal_entry: His pencil dropped. He couldn't draw anymore. He was looking at me — not the paper. The artist ran out of art. What was left was just a boy who wanted to touch what he'd been drawing for weeks.

nodes.name: Everything
nodes.journal_entry: I sent everything. All of me. He's coming to my room. Right now.

nodes.name: You Deserve This
nodes.journal_entry: The art show accepted three pieces. His first exhibition. I knelt by his chair. 'You deserve this.' He said I didn't have to. I know.

nodes.name: The Truth
nodes.journal_entry: 'I want to fuck you.' No art metaphor. No pretense. The sketchbook hit the floor. The bed is narrow. The wall is thin. We didn't care.

nodes.name: Three Inches
nodes.journal_entry: 2 AM. Kitchen. Whiskey. His hand on the table, three inches from mine. Neither of us moved closer. Neither of us moved away.

nodes.name: Forty Thousand
nodes.journal_entry: Found the real ledger. The business is $40,000 in debt. Frank doesn't know I know. Or does he?

nodes.name: Further
nodes.journal_entry: We went further. Past kissing, past pretending it's innocent. I knew what I was doing. I wanted to.

nodes.name: The Call
nodes.journal_entry: The business is failing. Client cancelled. Bank calling. Frank locked the office. 'Miss Chen.' Three days of cold. The steady man broke.

nodes.name: Come In
nodes.journal_entry: Three days of 'Miss Chen.' I knocked. 'Come in.' Two words. I sat beside him for the first time — same side of the desk. He didn't tell me to move.

nodes.name: The Wine
nodes.journal_entry: Wine. His office floor. He was talking about the mortgage and I looked down and saw what I'd been doing to him for a month. I didn't look away. I didn't want to.

nodes.name: The Coffee Mug Drawing
nodes.journal_entry: A drawing slid under my door. Not me — my coffee mug. The chip on the rim, the light on the ceramic. A detail only someone who watches constantly would notice. The drawing was the apology.

nodes.name: The Hallway
nodes.journal_entry: They found out. Both of them. The hallway at night, three feet wide, three people who can't pretend anymore. What I said next — or didn't say — changed everything.

nodes.name: The Bounce
nodes.journal_entry: Mom's transfer bounced. $47 in the bank. $185 in bills due. The math I've been outrunning finally caught me.

nodes.name: I'll Cover Everything
nodes.journal_entry: Frank's offer. Cover everything — bus, art supplies, phone, food. In exchange for... late nights. The office. 'Whatever I need help with.' We both know what that means.

nodes.name: She's Coming Home
nodes.journal_entry: Mom called. Flight booked. One week. Jake's pencil snapped. Ryan looked at the ceiling. Frank set down his fork. Very carefully.

nodes.name: Seven Days
nodes.journal_entry: Seven days. Every conversation is a last conversation. Every touch might be the final one. The countdown is real now.
